article_title: Learner Variability Is the Rule, Not the Exception
citation: Pape, B. (2018). Learner Variability Is the Rule, Not the Exception. Digital Promise Global. https://lvp.digitalpromiseglobal.org/
title: The Learner Variability Project four-pillar framework: Content, Cognition, Social and Emotional Learning, and Student Background
description: The Learner Variability Project (LVP) at Digital Promise distills learning sciences research into Learner Factors organized under four pillars: Content, Cognition, Social and Emotional Learning, and Student Background. Each Factor includes an explanation of what it is and how it connects with other Factors, situated in the context of a learning goal, with a robust list of research-based strategies showing how research may be applied in practice and product development.
requirements: Factors must be situated in the context of a learning goal, given the context principle of variability
Strategies must be research-based and complement the Factors
constraints: Current Learner Models cover Math pre-K to 2nd grade, Reading pre-K to 3rd grade, and Reading and Writing 4th-6th grade, with others in development
target_learners: teachers and edtech developers serving the full diversity of learners rather than a mythical average
target_learning_goals: putting research insights at educators' fingertips to infuse instruction or products with evidence-based resources
examples: LVP aims to expedite addressing each learner's variability by distilling research into a comprehensive yet brief and accessible form with example strategies
key_sources: Pape, B. (2018). Learner Variability Is the Rule, Not the Exception. Digital Promise Global. https://digitalpromise.dspacedirect.org/items/b7b14506-0b46-4279-9f9e-675c694b06a6

article_title: Using Videoconferencing Technology to Enhance Classroom Observation Methodology for the Instruction of Preservice Early Childhood Professionals
citation: Pickering, L. E., & Walsh, E. J. (2011). Using Videoconferencing Technology to Enhance Classroom Observation Methodology for the Instruction of Preservice Early Childhood Professionals. Journal of Digital Learning in Teacher Education, 27(3). https://iste.org
title: Internet-based videoconferencing observation setup with remote-controlled pan-tilt-zoom cameras and omnidirectional microphone
description: A low-cost, easy-to-operate videoconferencing installation enabling remote, unobtrusive classroom observation. The setup at the Child Study Center included "two remote-controlled cameras capable of panning, tilting, and zooming" and "one omnidirectional microphone," connected via Internet protocol to a campus multimedia classroom where the live feed is projected onto a large screen. Sessions can be recorded for make-up observations and to build a library of video segments.
requirements: Media consent from parents of observed children
A compatible videoconferencing system in the observing classroom
constraints: The system supports three additional camera inputs, which the authors suggest could address limited-view complaints
Sound quality during open-play periods was reported as poor
target_learning_goals: remote observation of preschool children's developmental behaviors
examples: The equipment was installed discreetly at a campus-based Child Study Center serving 3- and 4-year-olds, allowing a professor and class to observe inconspicuously
key_sources: Pickering, L. E., & Walsh, E. J. (2011). Using Videoconferencing Technology to Enhance Classroom Observation Methodology for the Instruction of Preservice Early Childhood Professionals. Journal of Digital Learning in Teacher Education, 27(3). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ918901
